A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VRoPE and contain readable text, equations, figures and tables. V2 includes Appendices A–E; v3 ends after the references. Relocated material and substantive omissions can be reliably distinguished.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, retrieval experiments, ablations, attention analyses and additional experiments in Appendices B and C.

after.justification: V3 retains original video-understanding, retrieval and ablation results in Tables 1–4 and attention visualizations in Figure 3.

M1.justification: Most of Section 4 reformulates the existing construction. However, v3's four positional streams correspond to v2's streams ordered 1,3,2,4, while both equations assign the listed order to successive j modulo 4 groups. Thus v3 Eq. 8 swaps two frequency assignments relative to v2 Eq. 9 as written. The frame stride H+W−1 and text encoding remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 retains the six main understanding benchmarks and Video-NIAH but removes EventBench's complex event-sequence evaluation and the OpenVid-1M training study from Appendix B. OneVision is newly listed for Qwen2 fine-tuning, although its additional domain coverage is unspecified. These changes remain within the existing video-language task scope.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain RoPE and RoPE-3D, plus RoPE-2D, RoPE-Share and RoPE-Compact in the variant ablation. Removed benchmark and backbone experiments use the same comparator set; no distinct comparison method disappears.

E3.justification: V3 removes the SigLIP-2/Qwen3-8B setting with 32 frames, 384×384 resolution, approximately 1M pre-training samples and 3M instruction-tuning samples, along with the eight-frame evaluation. This substantially reduces tested configuration diversity. Retained evaluations preserve the main 16-frame setup and Video-NIAH protocol. The revised Qwen2 training-source list does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 removes the boundary-attention diagnostic in v2 Table 1, duration-stratified Video-MME analysis in Table 7, sparse-frame robustness test in Table 8, and the query-specific attention/error case in Appendix C. These assessed mechanisms and failure conditions beyond aggregate accuracy. The main variant and component ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The tables' score differences relative to RoPE are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerical results in v2 Tables 2–5 are retained in v3 Tables 1–4. However, v3 removes boundary-attention measurements and all Appendix B/C results, including VRoPE's EventBench scores of 40.38, 54.23 and 60.35, eight-frame accuracy of 40.9, and Qwen3-8B average of 62.40. This is substantial result removal, without a reported performance improvement on retained evaluations.

T1.justification: The formal VRoPE definition changes its channel-associated positional ordering in v2 Eq. 9 versus v3 Eq. 8. Otherwise, the rotation/offset formulas largely refactor existing mathematics. Appendix A's dimensional-reduction argument moves to Section 4.3 with reordered coordinates. No theorem, proof or formal assumption is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now specify validation on Vicuna and Qwen2 at 1.5B/7B scales, replacing broader references to different models and training datasets. The central claims about spatial structure, attention bias, video-text continuity and improved video-task performance remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds an implicit temporal-modeling explanation. Section 5.3 removes v2's causal attribution of RoPE-3D's shorter-interval deficits to discontinuity and emphasizes extrapolation instead. Appendix robustness/error interpretations disappear, and the limitations now stop at 7B. V3 Table 2 also marks RoPE-2D as lacking continuity, contradicting the retained explanation that it resolves discontinuity.

D1.justification: The main learning rates, batch sizes, freezing strategy, pooling, hardware and promised code location remain. V3 removes Appendix D's explicit baseline-indexing examples, Appendix B.4's larger-model training recipe and Appendix E's research-only licensing disclosure. These reduce supplementary reproducibility information without establishing a change in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for Vicuna, Qwen2 and Su's 2024 multimodal-position discussion, while removing Qwen2.5-VL, EventBench, OpenVid-1M, SigLIP-2 and Qwen3 references. The substantive positioning against existing RoPE adaptations remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 is extensively rewritten and reordered from symmetry followed by temporal centering to rotation followed by symmetry. Component terminology changes throughout, Appendix A moves into a new Section 4.3, and Appendices B–E disappear. Together with revised introductory summaries, this substantially reorganizes the technical narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and v2's combined architecture/method Figure 3 becomes separate architecture and redesigned method figures in v3. The boundary-attention table, four appendix tables and diagnostic case figure are removed. The component-ablation table is relocated; the aggregate attention and retrieval heatmaps are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially weakens the empirical support for VRoPE's mechanisms and robustness by removing the boundary-attention diagnostic, duration and sparse-input analyses, EventBench evaluation, 8B scaling study and localization case without replacement measurements. The reorganized explanation and simpler method diagram improve accessibility, but do not offset this loss of validation. The new contradiction between Table 2 and Section 5.4 also reduces internal consistency.
